messages:
marta: Hey team — customer (acme-marketing) reports our API returning invalid JSON when they use structured_output=json_mode with a pydantic schema. They get a JSONDecodeError in their app. Posting sample response and curl they used.

marta: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <KEY>' 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
  -d '{"model":"gpt-xxl","json_mode":"structured","schema": {"type":"object","properties":{"title":{"type":"string"},"items":{"type":"array"}}},"prompt":"return object with title and items (strings)"}'

marta: Model output they received (copied raw):
```
{
  "title": "Weekly notes
",
  "items": [
    "point 1",
    "point 2",
  ], // trailing comma from model
}
```

marta: The customer's pydantic parse error: 
``nJSONDecodeError: Expecting property name enclosed in double quotes: line 5 column 3 (char 78)
``n
marta: They pasted the whole output into pydantic.parse_raw and it fails.

devon: ugh, trailing commas + unescaped control chars are a common model failure. :grimacing:

will: did they enable any postprocessing in the SDK? we recently added a 'sanitize_json_mode' flag in an internal branch but not released.

alicia: can you repro with our hosted model? share the exact request id and first/last ts from their call.

marta: request_id=rs_0a9c3f2, call_ts=2026-03-10T16:12:01Z. I tried `jq -R -s` locally and can reproduce the trailing comma + stray inline comment.

ryan: stray comments like `// trailing comma from model` is definitely coming from the assistant text, not a serializer. Some prompts encourage natural language commentary.

devon: reproduction steps for eng: 1) send same prompt, 2) capture streaming chunks, 3) concat. We should replicate their environment (they do parse_raw on full response).

marta: quick repro I ran: same curl -> got same invalid JSON. Pasting full response here: 
```
{"title":"Weekly notes
","items":["point 1","point 2",],}
```

marta: note the escaped newline inside title and trailing comma inside items.

will: two issues to unblock:
- user-facing workaround (support)
- engineering fix for structured parsing and clearer errors

alicia: Workaround suggestions: try using a tolerant parser that strips trailing commas and removes JS-style comments before handing to pydantic; or ask customer to use streaming and extract the first JSON fenced block.

devon: code snippet i use in local repro to sanitize: 
```python
import re, json
s = re.sub(r'//.*?\n', '\\n', raw)  # remove // comments
s = re.sub(r',\s*([\]}])', '\\1', s)  # remove trailing commas
obj = json.loads(s)
```

devon: not perfect but works for a lot of cases. we should ship this in SDK as an opt-in sanitizer.

marta: customer asked for root cause: why did model insert trailing comma and comment?

ryan: models often output 'human commentary' — when asked to include items they sometimes append commentary. In JSON mode we expect strictly formatted JSON but the model can still hallucinate extra punctuation.

will: Engineering idea: enforce a JSON-only decoder stage in the runtime that rejects non-JSON tokens during streaming and uses a small recovery heuristic (strip comment tokens, drop trailing commas) before returning the final string. If recovery fails, return a helpful error with sample of model output and suggestion to set 'json_mode=raw' or to add a stricter system prompt.

alicia: For immediate customer support I'll propose the sanitizer and share a short snippet. They can run it client-side.

marta: I've shared the snippet and asked if they want us to retry the request server-side. They said yes — please try a regenerate with a stricter prompt.

marta: regenerate returned clean JSON this time. I forwarded sanitized payload to customer and they were able to parse it with pydantic. :relieved:

alicia: tracking notes: add an automated test that injects comment tokens and trailing commas into streaming boundaries to ensure sanitizer handles chunk splits. Also tie parsing errors to the console's telemetry so we can find other customers.

ryan: fyi i'll add a blurb in docs: "If you see JSONDecodeError when using structured JSON mode: try our SDK's sanitize_json helper or add an explicit system instruction to avoid commentary and extra commas."

marta: closing loop with customer: they confirmed parsing succeeds after the regenerate+sandboxed sanitize. I'll mark the support ticket as "resolved pending monitoring".

marta: tl;dr: root cause = model producing human-style comments and trailing commas; short-term = client-side sanitizer + retry with stricter prompt; mid-term = runtime-level optional sanitizer + clearer JSONModeParseError in SDK.

marta: tagging eng-ml and SDK for follow up. :handshake:
